item.title: Fiji Airways launches 8-day anniversary sale to celebrate 75 years
item.description: From their first commercial flight taking off from Nausori on September 1st, 1951, bound for Drasa near Lautoka, to now operating a fleet of 23 aircraft and directly connecting Fiji to 37 destinations across 14 countries - that is the story of Fiji Airways as they celebrate their 75th anniversary today. item.content:encoded:
From their first commercial flight taking off from Nausori on September 1st, 1951, bound for Drasa near Lautoka, to now operating a fleet of 23 aircraft and directly connecting Fiji to 37 destinations across 14 countries - that is the story of Fiji Airways as they celebrate their 75th anniversary today.

As part of the celebration, Fiji Airways has launched an eight-day anniversary sale with special fares across its international network.

The anniversary sale runs from today until next Tuesday and covers destinations across Australia, New Zealand, the United States, Canada, Asia, Fiji, Samoa and Tonga.

Fiji Airways says the first three days of the promotion will feature its sharpest fares, followed by five days of special anniversary fares .

The promotional fares are available for travel from today to August 15th, 2027, although travel periods will vary depending on the market.

They say the promotion is available on selected flights and dates, with limited seats available at the promotional fares.

Customers are being encouraged to book early through the Fiji Airways website, sales offices, its 24/7 Reservations Call Centre or participating travel agents.

Peak-season travel restrictions and other conditions apply.

Through its oneworld membership, the airline says passengers can connect to more than 900 destinations worldwide.

item.title: Special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum on Online Safety to be held at 7pm Friday September 4th
item.description: A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm Friday September 4th. The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?
item.content:encoded:
A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm Friday September 4th.

The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?

The panelists for the public forum will be Online Safety Commissioner, Filipe Batiwale, Fiji Law Reform Commissioners David Solvalu and Valerie Narain.

The Straight Talk forum will focus on Online Safety Issues in Fiji, what is being faced by the Online Safety Commission, the feedback from the members of the public during the consultation process on the review of the Online Safety Act 2018, the call for age restrictions for Social Media, the response from victims, the changes being proposed and the reasons behind them amongst other issues.

You can also be part of the live audience by applying for registration with a question that you would like to ask during the forum.

The application to register details can be found on our website and facebook page, fijivillage.

You will receive a confirmation if you have been selected to be part of the live audience.

Please apply early to avoid any disappointment.

The show will be broadcast live at 7pm Friday September 4th on our Facebook, YouTube and X.

item.title: FTA questions Ministry of Education job advertisement over missing school details
item.description: FTA General Secretary Paula Manumanunitoga says the unions are disappointed with the Ministry's advertisement published on Saturday , August 29th. The Fiji Education Management Information System (FEMIS) is a web-based application developed by the Ministry of Education, Heritage and Arts (MoEHA) in Fiji.
item.content:encoded:
FTA General Secretary Paula Manumanunitoga says the unions are disappointed with the Ministry's advertisement published on Saturday , August 29th.

The Fiji Education Management Information System (FEMIS) is a web-based application developed by the Ministry of Education, Heritage and Arts (MoEHA) in Fiji.

He says interested applicants are unsure about which schools they want to apply to because key information about the advertised vacancies was not included.

Manumanunitoga is questioning why the complete list of schools could not have been included in the newspaper advertisement instead of requiring teachers to access FEMIS for further details.

He says many aspiring and eligible candidates could miss out if they face internet connectivity issues and are unable to access FEMIS.

The FTA General Secretary says this is particularly concerning as teachers are currently on school holidays, with some spending their break in villages and maritime areas where internet access may be limited.

He says requiring teachers to cross-reference FEMIS unnecessarily complicates the process and is calling on the Ministry to simplify it by publishing complete advertisements containing the school names, locations, post advertisement numbers and other relevant details.

fijivillage News has contacted the Ministry of Education for a response.

item.title: Lionel Richie hospitalized after St. Louis concert
item.description: Grammy Award-winning singer and songwriter Lionel Richie checked himself into a St. Louis hospital after his concert at The Muny over the weekend, according to reports. TMZ, which first reported Lionel's hospitalization, says the singer appeared to struggle toward the end of Saturday night’s performance and requested a chair during the final song, “All Night Long.”
item.content:encoded:
Grammy Award-winning singer and songwriter Lionel Richie checked himself into a St. Louis hospital after his concert at The Muny over the weekend, according to reports.

TMZ, which first reported Lionel's hospitalization, says the singer appeared to struggle toward the end of Saturday night’s performance and requested a chair during the final song, “All Night Long.”

ABC News also confirmed that Richie went to the hospital as a precaution.

A source told Rolling Stone that the singer is doing well.

item.title: More than 50 solar streetlights installed in Tailevu
item.description: The project is being carried out by the Yavusa Tai Development Fund and is financed by the Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany. The project will see solar streetlights installed in four villages in the Namalata District.
item.content:encoded:
The project is being carried out by the Yavusa Tai Development Fund and is financed by the Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany.

The project will see solar streetlights installed in four villages in the Namalata District.

So far, 22 solar streetlights have been installed in Nakalawaca Village, located behind the old Fulton College, while 30 streetlights have been installed in Matacaucau Village.

Work has also started in Veinuqa Village as part of the wider Namalata District Solar Streetlights Project yesterday.

The Mata ni Tikina of Namalata Ilatia Savai says the solar streetlights will greatly assist villagers, particularly at night, and provide greater safety for children moving around the communities.

He says the villages are grateful for the assistance and the improvements the project is bringing to their communities.
